The first and third absolute row sums are bounded below by 1+t(c+d) and (1+t)[1-t(c+d)]; the crossing of these affine lines yields the matching global lower bound. When 0<t<1 equality forces d=0,c=1/(2+t) and unique a,b in this symmetry class. Injectivity of ℓ∞⁴ transfers the relative projection norm to the absolute constant. An explicit invertible map T_t provides d≤1+t/2, while λ≤d; the sandwich proves derivative 1/2. Independent 25-variable *non-equivariant* linear programs at seven t parameters attained the stated global minimum and verified sharpness beyond equivariance.
